lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

The Direct3D mend passed. Decision 265. Its whole report came at 9:04 PM MT Friday and was read whole here. Stated and measured by its builder, the branch head read back here: 17 files against the main branch, all eight guard stills equal to the list in force on five heads and twelve film frames equal, so no picture moves on Linux; the whole test run 1076 passed and 8 skipped in 74 files. Stated from a hosted Windows machine without a graphics card, Chrome through Direct3D 11, 13 film frames: 114 programs linked with 0 errors; the compiler no longer leaves out the tests for a broken number (before 24 times), no longer warns of a read inside a loop (before in 42 programs), and its caution on a value that may not be set stays in one place only, fall's leaf cards, left on purpose by decision 259 (open item 282). A probe on that machine answers the new test for a broken number with yes for both kinds. One compiler notice stays in summer's glass, that its optimization did not converge; the program links. The report also names a gap that no list has closed: the programs made only at the masters' quality, for pieces in flight in a storm and for the travelling globe, have never been through Microsoft's compiler, because the hosted job draws one sample a frame. Ruled: a last part, due by 10:40 PM MT. Those programs go through the builder's own copy of Microsoft's compiler here, an error is reported at once, and the count of broken pixels is made to see a dropped sample again so that the gate that reads it does not go blind. The branch lands last in chain 44.

The stall at low quality: floor 5 pushed at 9:05 PM MT, read whole here, its two sheets of the pushed head looked at. Measured by its builder: on the pushed head, in two of the eight arms, 130 of 130 pictured states of the controls are the same in every pixel as the main branch's; on the same sheets before the last merge all eight arms, 336 of 336. The whole test run 1075 passed and 8 skipped in 72 files, the eight guard stills equal, 45 of 45 planted faults caught by its tests. The named presses on the software renderer at low quality: before the mend 2 of 16 presses with a second stall, longest 1293 ms; with it 0 of 16, longest 100 ms. Said plainly by it and open: a press on the menu's options still stalls on the software renderer, 4 of 8 presses in one walk, longest 5098 ms. The menu's sheet is the main branch's own and the same walk on the main branch is not measured yet; it is owed with floor 6, the low quality's point sprites on the merged tree, due by 9:55 PM MT. A real graphics card has not been seen.

The final render on his own computer. Decision 264. The short test drew winter at rest and spring just landed at 3840x2160 at the masters' quality on a hosted Windows machine through Direct3D 11 on Microsoft's software card, 49 minutes, and passed against the cloud's references (measured by that run): 41.42 dB and 42.88 dB on the whole picture, the glass's brightness 0.3037 against 0.3043 and 0.7154 against 0.7155. The first picture attached is its sheet, the cloud's reference left and what Windows drew right. Seen here: the two sides look alike, the differences lie on the table's shine and the snow lumps. The tolerance is taken as built. Unknown: any real graphics card, and whether Windows draws fall's leaves with their veins; a still for that is ordered from the hosted Windows machine and the release line for the final render stays off until it is seen. No final render is started in the cloud.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. Chain 44: the stall's mend with the point sprites (floor 6 due by 9:55 PM MT), summer's fireflies and the seeds' dots (first report due by 9:25 PM MT, second by 10:50 PM MT), the frost line at film frame 668 (report due about 10:35 PM MT), the Direct3D mend last (its last part due by 10:40 PM MT), as each passes. Then a critic for the change of season and a fifteenth publish. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, then a cold read by a fresh critic. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard and BUILD COMPLETE.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker. Summer's pond at rest (item 279). Fall's storm paler than approved. Spring's glass after a shake pale on pale, with square corners at the lower ends of a few runs. Spring's fence and trails. The fireflies' flat bars at 4K (item 276). The seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277). The sand of the petals' mend at 4K before the encode, one small petal's softer edge and the petals' fringe at film frames 681 and 682 (item 278). The frost line at film frame 668 (item 275). The stall at low quality on a software renderer, until chain 44, and after it still at the menu's options. One compiler caution on Windows at fall's leaf cards (item 282). The square pressed fill of one menu option (item 283). One level in 14 corner pixels of the menu on a starved machine (item 284). Winter's four small items. Fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272). The poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273). Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, sound heard by a person.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
